record.context_brief: double-barrier Luttinger-liquid conductance from form factors
record.original_question: In a Luttinger liquid with two barriers, after integrating out small island-charge fluctuations in the weak-barrier limit to obtain an effective boundary action with a relevant cos(2√πθ) term of strength aV and an irrelevant cos(4√πθ) term of strength bV^2/(2M), what is the conductance as a function of the effective couplings a and b, and how can the required form factors for the irrelevant perturbation be obtained?

evidence.quote: In the opposite, weak barrier limit, V ≪ M, following Kane and Fisher one can integrate out small fluctuations of the charge around the value hni and obtain an effective action.
The second cosine term in the last formula is irrelevant for g > 1/4, while the first one is relevant.
It is interesting to find the conductance as a function of a, b by the form-factor method, treating one of the cosine terms in (58) as perturbation.

In the third problem one has to deal with the irrelevant perturbation, for which the form-factors are not quite known. One can in principle overcome this difficulty by an analytic continuation from the space of relevant perturbations.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a spinless Luttinger liquid with Luttinger parameter g containing two identical weak barriers that enclose an island. In the weak-barrier regime, after integrating out small fluctuations of the island charge around its mean value, the low-energy effective boundary action for the dual field θ(τ) takes the form

  S_eff = S_LL[θ] + ∫ dτ [ aV cos(2√π θ(τ)) + (bV^2/(2M)) cos(4√π θ(τ)) ],

where V is the bare barrier strength, M is the island charging energy, and a, b are dimensionless constants determined by the microscopic integration over island-charge fluctuations. For g > 1/4 the operator cos(2√π θ) is renormalization-group relevant while cos(4√π θ) is irrelevant.

(1) Compute the linear-response DC conductance G(a,b) of this double-barrier setup as a function of the couplings a and b (and of g, the temperature/voltage scale, etc.), via the form-factor expansion of the boundary sine-Gordon-like theory, treating one cosine term as the perturbation.

(2) Determine the form factors required for the irrelevant cos(4√π θ) perturbation. In particular, propose and justify a method (e.g., analytic continuation from the space of relevant perturbations) that produces these form factors and allows one to evaluate the conductance contributions from the irrelevant term.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches on double-barrier Luttinger-liquid conductance via form factors with both relevant and irrelevant boundary cosine perturbations return general reviews and works on transport through double barriers and nonperturbative RG approaches, but no source that explicitly provides the form-factor computation of G(a,b) using analytic continuation from the relevant sector to the irrelevant cos(4√π θ) perturbation. The status of this specific question is not clearly established by the search results.

status_evidence.title: Transport of interacting electrons through a potential barrier: nonperturbative RG approach
status_evidence.snippet: Nonperturbative RG approach to transport through a barrier in Luttinger liquids; does not address form-factor computation for the irrelevant cos(4√π θ) perturbation.
status_evidence.claim: Related work treats barrier transport via RG, not the requested form-factor evaluation.

status_evidence.title: Coherent transport of charge through a double barrier in a Luttinger liquid (Phys. Rev. B 52, 11213)
status_evidence.snippet: Kane-Fisher style treatment of double-barrier transport in a Luttinger liquid.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the effective action setup but not the form-factor conductance G(a,b).
